x.around: Papeete is a walking town. Drivers stop for pedestrians at crosswalks (zebra crossings). It's really too small to bother with any other form of transport, unless you are going out to the fringes, or would simply like to experience the famous le truck for fun (hop-on, hop-off, anywhere in the city centre for about 100 F) Bring a water bottle: it can be quite hot and humid.

hidden.d: A museum displaying exhibits on pearl farming and the history of pearls on one side and a pearl shop on the other.

n.fr: musée de la perle de Tahiti

x.intro: Papeete is the largest city in and capital of French Polynesia on the island of Tahiti.

must.d: The Catholic cathedral built in the 19th century

n.es: catedral de Nuestra Señora de Papeete

intro: French Polynesia (French: Polynésie française) is a collection of over 100 islands in the South Pacific Ocean, halfway between California and Australia. It is an overseas country (pays d'outre-mer), the only French territory with this status.

other.d: far to the east, closer to Mexico, is administered directly by the Ministry of Overseas France

x.around: There are no other means of transportation on Clipperton Island than your own feet, and walking on the island is quite difficult. You will encounter two types of surfaces. One is soft sand, which collapses under your feet due to the burrows dug by the island's many crabs. The other surface is made out of hard coral fragments cemented together, covered with loose coral pieces.
x.intro: Clipperton Island (French: Île de Clipperton), also known as Île de la Passion is a small, ring-shaped atoll located 1,120 km southwest of Mexico in the Pacific Ocean. It has no permanent residents and is mainly visited by Mexican fishermen and French Navy patrols.
x.safe: The heat, the sun and the lack of water will be your worst enemies, so bring enough to drink, plenty of sunscreen and some good sunglasses against the bright light. Also be aware that the island is subject to extremely heavy rain and vicious tropical storms.

x.around: The roads consist of mostly dirt and the weather is for the most, tropical.
x.intro: Rapa is a remote atoll in the Austral Islands of French Polynesia with a population of about 500. It is also known as Rapa Iti or Oparo. It is not to be confused with Rapa Nui (Easter Island).
